> On May 10, 2017, at 6:07 PM, Sean Pinkney <sean.p...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Gelman has a post on lasso regression in Stan. However, I'm wondering if we can do penalized regression with ordinal predictors (paper link) for a logistic regression?

You can't implement the Lasso log density, but it's not continuously
differentiable and we can't find the zero the same way something
like a truncated gradient descent can.

Did you want to enforce some sort of behavior on the coefficients
for the ordinal predictors? If you're sure of the direction and
ordering of effects, you can use an ordered vector. Usually you
want K - 1 effects for K categories to aid with identifiability.
Otherwise, you'll be relying very heavily on priors for identifiability.

- Bob


> Basically, I have a number of logistic regressions with ordinal variates which sometimes fail due to low sample on some of the levels of the ordinal variate. So, I could use the ordPens package in R (link). But, the model has a random intercept and random slopes specification with the groups (x6-8 in the example below) so I think a hierarchical penalized logistic regression makes the most sense.
>
> For example
>
> Outcome:
> y ~ binomial
>
> Ordinal predictors
> x1 - income (coded as 1 - 7)
> x2 - age (coded as 1 - 5)
>
> Categorical predictors
> x3 - gender (coded as 0, 1)
>
> Continuous
> x4 - positive real number
> x5 - positive real number
>
> group indicators (observation can be in more than one group)
> x6 - 1,0
> x7 - 1,0
> x8 - 1,0
>
> Thanks for any help or thoughts!
>
> Sean
